catalog.name: Topography
catalog.description: Digital elevation models and topographic datasets providing essential context for hydrological analysis, terrain modeling, and watershed delineation.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: HydroSHEDS data: Lehner, B., Verdin, K., Jarvis, A. (2008): New global hydrography derived from spaceborne elevation data. Eos, Transactions, AGU, 89(10): 93-94. Data distributed by WWF and McGill University.

info.name: License
info.content: HydroSHEDS data available for non-commercial use. For commercial applications, contact the HydroSHEDS team.

info.name: Applications
info.content: Watershed delineation, hydrological modeling, terrain analysis, flood risk assessment, and environmental studies.

members.name: HydroSHEDS Global 30s Void-filled DEM
members.description:
Global digital elevation model at 30 arc-second resolution (~1 km) from the HydroSHEDS dataset, void-filled for hydrological applications.

Dataset URL: https://www.hydrosheds.org/hydrosheds-core-downloads

info.name: Background
info.content: The HydroSHEDS DEM is derived from NASA's Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) data and has been specifically processed for hydrological applications. Void areas in the original SRTM data have been filled using auxiliary elevation datasets to provide complete global coverage.

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 30 arc-seconds (~1 km at the equator), global coverage between 60°N and 60°S

info.name: Data Processing
info.content: The DEM has been hydrologically conditioned through void-filling, sink removal, and stream network enforcement to ensure proper flow routing for hydrological modeling applications.

info.name: Methodology
info.content: Created from SRTM C-band radar data with additional processing including void-filling using ASTER GDEM, GTOPO30, and other elevation sources. Hydrological conditioning ensures drainage networks flow properly to ocean outlets.

info.name: Applications
info.content: Watershed delineation, flow direction mapping, stream network extraction, flood modeling, and any hydrological analysis requiring terrain data.

info.name: Data Format
info.content: Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) format for efficient web-based visualization and analysis

info.name: Attribution
info.content: HydroSHEDS by Lehner, B., Verdin, K., Jarvis, A. Based on SRTM data from NASA/JPL-Caltech and NGA. Distributed by WWF-US and McGill University.
